root_cause.text: `memcg_alloc_abort_single()` in `mm/slub.c` failed to call `alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook()` when `__memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook()` aborted a single-object allocation, leaving alloc_tag state uncleared and causing stale profiling tags to persist into the next allocation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `struct slab *slab = virt_to_slab(object);` and an explicit `alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook(s, slab, &object, 1);` call at the start of `memcg_alloc_abort_single()`, and the commit message says the warning occurs because “in memcg_alloc_abort_single() we don't” call the free hook, unlike the `kmem_cache_free_bulk()` path, so “the above warning will be triggered on the next allocation.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Cache the slab pointer and invoke alloc tagging before aborting a memcg allocation free path.
intent_record.what: In memcg_alloc_abort_single(), a local struct slab *slab is introduced and initialized with virt_to_slab(object), alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook() is called before the free path, and the later do_slab_free() call is changed to reuse the cached slab pointer instead of calling virt_to_slab(object) again.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now performs slab-related free tagging before attempting the slab free hook, and it avoids recomputing the slab pointer on the free path by using the already-derived slab value. This changes the ordering of free-accounting/tagging work and makes the free operation use a consistent slab reference.

grouping_result.intent: Cache the slab pointer and invoke alloc tagging before aborting a memcg allocation free path.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly mentions invoking alloc tagging before aborting the memcg allocation free path, which matches the root cause of missing alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook() on aborted single-object memcg slab allocations.

candidates.rationale: This is the conditional in the abort path that directly leads to freeing the object without any alloc-tag cleanup on the single-object abort path. Because the pre-fix code jumps straight from this check to do_slab_free(), the alloc_tag state is never cleared when __memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook() aborts allocation.

This is the abort/free operation executed by memcg_alloc_abort_single() in the vulnerable code path. It returns the object to the slab without first invoking alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook(), which leaves stale alloc-tag information attached to the next allocation.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the abort/free operation in memcg_alloc_abort_single(). In the vulnerable code path, it returns the object to the slab immediately after the slab_free_hook check, but before any alloc tagging cleanup occurs, so stale alloc_tag state remains uncleared when __memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook() aborts a single-object allocation.

This conditional gates the vulnerable abort path. When it succeeds, the code proceeds directly to do_slab_free() without calling alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook(), which is the missing cleanup that caused stale profiling tags to persist into the next allocation.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 9f9796b413d3c417f34cae427c4e47bfdd3a7454
Author: Vlastimil Babka <vbabka@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Mar 26 11:37:38 2024 +0100

    mm, slab: move memcg charging to post-alloc hook
    
    Patch series "memcg_kmem hooks refactoring", v3.
    
    
    This patch (of 2):
    
    The MEMCG_KMEM integration with slab currently relies on two hooks during
    allocation.  memcg_slab_pre_alloc_hook() determines the objcg and charges
    it, and memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook() assigns the objcg poin
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code already contains the abort path for single-object memcg post-allocation failure, and it explicitly calls the free/cleanup hook. In `memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook()`, after a failed post-alloc check it does `if (likely(size == 1)) { memcg_alloc_abort_single(s, *p); *p = NULL; }`, and `memcg_alloc_abort_single()` is defined later as `if (likely(slab_free_hook(s, object, slab_want_init_on_free(s)))) do_slab_free(...);`. This is the correct cleanup path for a single object. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is the absence of `alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook()` in `memcg_alloc_abort_single()`, but that hook is not present in this snippet at all, so the specific bug cannot be observed here. Since the visible code already has the abort/free handling inserted, it reflects the fix rather than the bug.

Author: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Date:   Fri Aug 9 17:36:56 2024 +0200

    slub: Introduce CONFIG_SLUB_RCU_DEBUG
    
    Currently, KASAN is unable to catch use-after-free in SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU
    slabs because use-after-free is allowed within the RCU grace period by
    design.
    
    Add a SLUB debugging feature which RCU-delays every individual
    kmem_cache_free() before either actually freeing the object or handing it
    off to KA
bic_trace_step.reason:
The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is specifically that `memcg_alloc_abort_single()` failed to call `alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook()` when aborting a single-object allocation, leaving alloc_tag state uncleared. In this snippet, `memcg_alloc_abort_single()` is shown as:

`static noinline void memcg_alloc_abort_single(struct kmem_cache *s, void *object) { if (likely(slab_free_hook(s, object, slab_want_init_on_free(s), false))) do_slab_free(s, virt_to_slab(object), object, object, 1, _RET_IP_); }`

There is no call to `alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook()` in this function body, but crucially the function itself is just part of a larger free path and the snippet does not show whether alloc-tag cleanup is expected to happen elsewhere for this path. However, based on the shown code alone, the specific vulnerable omission is not present as an explicitly visible bug in this function body beyond the absence of that hook call; this commit is about introducing CONFIG_SLUB_RCU_DEBUG and the function is not showing the alloc-tag fix logic. Therefore the shown function does not contain the vulnerable construct in a way that can be attributed here, and it also does not show the fix.
